topics.name: langgraph.json and Application Structure
topics.description: Configuration keys, dependencies, graphs, environment variables and HTTP settings of a deployable app.
notes: ## langgraph.json 配置
- langgraph.json 描述部署所需的 dependencies、graphs、环境变量等；CLI 默认读取当前目录下的 langgraph.json。
- 一个应用由四部分组成：配置文件、图（graphs）、依赖文件（requirements.txt / pyproject.toml / package.json）、环境变量。
```json
"dependencies": ["."],
"graphs": {"support_agent": "./my_agent/support.py:agent", "research_agent": "./my_agent/research.py:agent"},
"env": "./.env"
- dependencies：可以是 "."、包含依赖文件的目录路径（如 "./"）或包名；不要写 "requirements.txt" 文件名本身。
- graphs：图 ID 到 "文件:变量" 或 "文件:函数" 的映射；同一部署可定义多个图，它们共享 dependencies、env 和镜像。
- 每个图会得到一个默认 assistant，客户端用图 ID 作为 assistant_id 来选择图。
- env：.env 文件路径或变量映射，主要用于本地运行；生产环境通常在部署环境中配置变量和密钥。
- python_version（3.11/3.12/3.13）、image_distro（debian/wolfi/bookworm/bullseye）、api_version 用来固定运行环境。
- source: {"kind": "uv"} 会按 uv.lock 安装锁定版本；此时要省略 dependencies，并设置 python_version。
- 只写 "dependencies": ["."] 时，构建会根据 pyproject.toml 重新解析版本，不使用 uv.lock。
- http 块可配置 cors、middleware_order、configurable_headers、disable_meta 等；auth、store、checkpointer 也在同一文件中配置。
- disable_meta 会关闭 /、/info、/metrics、/docs、/openapi.json，但 /ok 健康检查保留，Kubernetes 探针仍可使用。

topics.name: LangGraph CLI, Local Server and Studio
topics.description: langgraph dev, up, build, dockerfile, SDK access and Studio for local development.
notes: ## 本地开发与 Studio
- LangGraph CLI 的常用命令：dev、build、deploy、dockerfile、up。
- langgraph dev：无需 Docker 的轻量服务，支持热重载，状态保存在本地目录，默认端口 2024；需要安装 langgraph-cli[inmem]。
- langgraph up：在 Docker 中启动完整栈（API 服务、PostgreSQL、Redis），默认端口 8123，更接近生产环境。
```bash
pip install -U "langgraph-cli[inmem]"
langgraph dev
langgraph up --recreate
- 推荐流程：日常用 dev 迭代 → 定期用 up 验证 → 部署前用 up --recreate 全新构建 → 部署。
- langgraph build -t <tag> 构建 Agent Server 的 Docker 镜像（-t 必填）。
- langgraph dockerfile 根据配置生成 Dockerfile；修改 langgraph.json 后需要重新生成。
- 依赖安装出问题时，可在配置中设置 "pip_installer": "pip"，然后重新构建。
- 用 langgraph-sdk 的 get_client / get_sync_client 连接本地服务；runs.stream(None, "agent", ...) 表示不绑定线程的运行。
- Studio 是可视化、交互并调试 agent 的 IDE，可连接本地服务或已部署的图。
- Graph 模式展示节点和中间状态；Chat 模式更简洁，仅支持状态包含或扩展 MessagesState 的图。
- Studio 还可以管理 assistants 与 threads、迭代 prompt，并通过 time travel 调试状态。

topics.name: Deployment Options, Revisions and RemoteGraph
topics.description: Cloud, hybrid, self-hosted and standalone options, revisions, and calling deployments from clients.
notes: ## 部署方式与客户端接入
- LangSmith Deployment 与框架无关，所有环境使用同一个 Agent Server 运行时。
- Cloud：由 LangChain 在 AWS/GCP 上全托管，可从 GitHub 或 langgraph deploy 创建，需要 Plus 及以上套餐。
- Self-hosted with control plane：控制平面和 Agent Server 都在自己的 Kubernetes 集群中运行（需要 Enterprise）。
- Hybrid：控制平面由 LangChain 托管，Agent Server 和数据平面在自己的基础设施中。
- Standalone server：用 Docker、Compose 或 Kubernetes 部署，自备 PostgreSQL、Redis 和 license，没有控制平面。
- Cloud 部署类型：Serverless 可能有冷启动；Dedicated 提供常驻容量（langgraph deploy --deployment-type dedicated）。
## Revision
- 创建部署时产生第一个 revision；之后通过 UI 的 + New Revision 或再次运行 langgraph deploy 发布新 revision。
- langgraph deploy 只能更新最初由它创建的部署；通过 UI 或 GitHub 集成创建的部署需用 UI 更新。
- 使用自己管理的 registry 时用 --push-to，或用 --image-uri 部署已推送的镜像（必须带 @sha256 摘要，不能用可变 tag）。
## RemoteGraph
- RemoteGraph 让你像调用本地编译图一样调用已部署的图：invoke、stream、get_state 等方法一致。
```python
from langgraph.pregel.remote import RemoteGraph
remote_graph = RemoteGraph("agent", url="<DEPLOYMENT_URL>")
- name 可以是图名（使用默认 assistant）或 assistant ID；需要 LangSmith API key。
- 默认运行是无状态的；要持久化状态，需创建 thread 并通过 config 传入 thread_id。
- 不要用 RemoteGraph 调用同一部署上的图，可能导致死锁；同一部署内应使用本地组合或子图。

topics.name: LangSmith Monitoring, Alerts, Rules and Cost
topics.description: Dashboards, alerts, automation rules and cost tracking in LangSmith.
notes: ## LangSmith 监控与成本
- Prebuilt dashboard 会为每个 tracing project（或 agent environment）自动创建，包含 Traces、LLM Calls、Cost & Tokens、Tools、Run Types、Feedback Scores 等部分。
- 可按 run tag 或 metadata 分组；metadata 和 tags 不会在父子 run 之间传播，需要在 trace 和具体 run 上各自附加。
- Custom dashboard 的指标：Count、Latency、Time to first token、Tokens、Cost、Feedback score、Ratio；Ratio 由分子和分母（各自带 filter）组成，可用于错误率。
## Alerts
- Alerts 作用于单个 tracing project 或 agent environment，基于阈值；指标类型有 Run Count、Cost、Errors、Feedback Score、Latency。
- 条件包括聚合方法、比较运算符、阈值和聚合窗口（5 或 15 分钟）；Errors 与 Latency 还可用 filter（Status、Run Type、Tag、Error），条件之间只支持 AND。
- 通知渠道：Slack、PagerDuty、Dynatrace、Webhook。
- Webhook 不做模板替换；告警字段（alert_rule_name、project_name、triggered_metric_value 等）作为顶层键并入 JSON。
## Automation rules
- 规则由 item type（Runs/Threads）、filter、sampling rate 和 action 定义。
- Action 包括 Add to Annotation Queue、Add to Dataset、Trigger Webhooks、在线评估器、Extend Data Retention 等。
- Thread 规则在线程空闲后才执行，空闲时间默认 10 分钟，不能低于 2 分钟。
## Cost tracking
- LLM 成本由 token 数、模型与提供商（ls_provider、ls_model_name）和模型价格表自动计算。
- 非线性定价或非 LLM run（如 tool）可在 usage_metadata 中直接给出成本，例如 total_cost。
```python
run = get_current_run_tree()
run.set(usage_metadata={"total_cost": 0.0015})
- 价格表的更新不会回填已经记录的 trace。

questions.title: Which configuration file does the LangGraph CLI use by default?
questions.explanation: The CLI defaults to langgraph.json in the current directory; the -c/--config option can point to another path. The .env file only holds environment variables and is referenced from langgraph.json.

questions.title: The project keeps its dependencies in requirements.txt at the repository root, but the build cannot find them. What is the documented fix for this langgraph.json?

options.text: Rename the graphs key to requirements
Turn env into an object instead of a file path
Use "./", the directory that contains requirements.txt, instead of the file name

questions.explanation: dependencies takes a directory path (or "." or a package name) where the dependency file lives; the docs say not to specify the string requirements.txt itself. The other changes do not affect how dependencies are located.

questions.title: langgraph.json defines two graphs. Which value completes the call so that the research graph runs?
questions.codeSnippet:
# langgraph.json graphs:
#   "support_agent": "./my_agent/support.py:agent"
#   "research_agent": "./my_agent/research.py:agent"
from langgraph_sdk import get_client

client = get_client(url="http://localhost:2024")

async def run_research():
    async for chunk in client.runs.stream(
        None, "______", input={"messages": [{"role": "human", "content": "Hi"}]}
    ):
        print(chunk.event)
questions.explanation: Agent Server creates a default assistant per graph, so the graph ID from the graphs key is passed as the assistant_id. The file path is the value of the key, not the ID.

questions.title: Which values are valid for the image_distro key of langgraph.json?
questions.explanation: The documented options are debian, wolfi, bookworm and bullseye, with wolfi recommended for smaller and more secure images. alpine is not listed.

questions.title: The project has a uv.lock and image builds must install the locked versions. Which key completes the config?
questions.explanation: source with kind "uv" makes the build export requirements from the lockfile (uv export --frozen) and requires python_version. pip_installer only selects the installer and does not control whether uv.lock is used.

questions.title: Which routes are disabled when langgraph.json sets "http": {"disable_meta": true}?
questions.explanation: disable_meta turns off /, /info, /metrics, /docs and /openapi.json. The /ok health check stays available for liveness and readiness probes, and thread routes are controlled by a separate disable_threads flag.

questions.title: How does the application-structure documentation say environment variables are typically handled for a production deployment, compared with local runs?

options.text: They must always be hard-coded in langgraph.json
They are not supported in production
They are read from the graph state at runtime
The env key is used for local runs, while production variables are typically configured in the deployment environment

questions.explanation: The env key of langgraph.json is convenient when running a deployed-style app locally, but for production you typically configure variables and secrets in the deployment environment itself.

questions.title: Which command starts a lightweight local Agent Server without requiring Docker?
questions.explanation: langgraph dev runs directly in your environment with hot reloading and no Docker. langgraph up needs Docker and starts the full container stack.

questions.title: On which port does langgraph dev listen by default?
questions.explanation: langgraph dev defaults to port 2024, while langgraph up defaults to 8123. Port 5432 is used by the PostgreSQL container started by langgraph up.

questions.title: Which extra must be installed so that the langgraph dev command is available?
questions.explanation: The dev server requires the inmem extra of langgraph-cli. The other names are not documented extras.

questions.title: Which statements about langgraph dev and langgraph up are correct?

options.text: langgraph up persists state in PostgreSQL
langgraph dev reloads on code changes by default
langgraph dev requires a PostgreSQL container
langgraph dev listens on port 8123 by default

questions.explanation: up builds and runs containers for the server, PostgreSQL and Redis, while dev is a lightweight in-environment server with hot reloading. dev uses port 2024 and needs no database container.

questions.title: What do the first two positional arguments of runs.stream mean in this call?
questions.codeSnippet:
from langgraph_sdk import get_sync_client

client = get_sync_client(url="http://localhost:2024")

for chunk in client.runs.stream(
    None,
    "agent",
    input={"messages": [{"role": "human", "content": "Hi"}]},
    stream_mode="messages-tuple",
):
    print(chunk.event)

options.text: None selects the default thread; "agent" is the Docker image name
None is a threadless run; "agent" is the assistant (graph) name defined in langgraph.json
None disables streaming; "agent" is the API key
None is the checkpoint ID; "agent" is the node name

questions.explanation: Passing None as the thread makes a threadless run, and the second argument is the assistant, which can be the graph name from langgraph.json. It is not an image, key or node name.

questions.title: For which graphs does Studio's Chat mode work?

options.text: Any graph, regardless of its state schema
Only graphs whose state includes or extends MessagesState
Only graphs deployed to LangSmith Cloud

questions.explanation: Chat mode is a simpler UI that requires a messages-based state. Graph mode exposes the full feature set, and Studio works with both local and deployed graphs.

questions.title: The image build fails because uv cannot resolve this project's dependency graph. Which change is the documented fix?

options.text: Set pip_installer to "pip" and rebuild, for example with langgraph up --recreate

questions.explanation: pip_installer can be switched to pip when uv cannot handle the dependency graph or pyproject structure, and a fresh rebuild applies it. The other options are unrelated to dependency installation or are invalid values.

questions.title: You generated a Dockerfile with langgraph dockerfile and later edited langgraph.json. What is required for the change to take effect when building that Dockerfile?

options.text: Nothing; the Dockerfile reads langgraph.json at build time
Run langgraph dockerfile again to regenerate it

questions.explanation: The command translates langgraph.json into Dockerfile instructions at generation time, so later edits are not reflected until it is re-run.

questions.title: Which LangSmith Deployment option runs Agent Server containers that you manage yourself with Docker or Kubernetes and has no control plane?
questions.explanation: A standalone Agent Server needs your own PostgreSQL, Redis and LangSmith license and has no control plane. The other options all include a control plane, managed by LangChain or by you.

questions.title: Which are LangSmith Deployment environments described in the docs?
questions.explanation: The docs list Cloud, Self-hosted with control plane, Hybrid and Standalone server, all using the same Agent Server runtime. No mobile on-device option exists.

questions.title: What does RemoteGraph provide?

options.text: A tool for visualizing graphs in the browser
A client-side interface to call a deployment like a local compiled graph, with methods such as invoke() and stream()
A way to bundle the graph into a Docker image

questions.explanation: RemoteGraph offers API parity with a compiled graph so the same code works against a local graph and a deployment. It does not build images or store data itself.

questions.title: Why can get_state(config) return the state of the earlier invoke() call in this code?
questions.codeSnippet:
from langgraph.pregel.remote import RemoteGraph
from langgraph_sdk import get_sync_client

url = "<DEPLOYMENT_URL>"
remote_graph = RemoteGraph("agent", url=url)
thread = get_sync_client(url=url).threads.create()
config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": thread["thread_id"]}}
remote_graph.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}, config=config)
print(remote_graph.get_state(config))

options.text: RemoteGraph always persists every run on its own
get_state works with just the graph name
A thread was created and its thread_id was passed through config; runs without a thread are stateless by default

questions.explanation: By default runs are stateless; passing a thread ID in config makes the deployment persist checkpoints and state for that thread. Persistence is not automatic and does not depend on the URL.

questions.title: Why should RemoteGraph not be used to call another graph on the same deployment?

options.text: RemoteGraph cannot call graphs that use a checkpointer
It is only supported in JavaScript
It always requires a different API key
It can cause deadlocks and resource exhaustion; use local graph composition or subgraphs instead

questions.explanation: The docs warn that RemoteGraph is meant for graphs on other deployments, and calling the same deployment can deadlock. Graphs within one deployment should be composed locally or as subgraphs.

questions.title: You ran langgraph deploy earlier to create a Cloud deployment. What happens when you run langgraph deploy again from the project directory after changing code?

options.text: A second, separate deployment is always created
It finds the existing deployment by name and creates a new revision with the latest code
It deletes the deployment and starts over
It only updates the environment variables

questions.explanation: Revisions release code changes to an existing deployment; langgraph deploy locates the deployment by name (or --deployment-id) and adds a revision. It can only update deployments originally created with langgraph deploy.

questions.title: Which automation rule action sends matching traces to humans for review?
questions.explanation: Add to Annotation Queue places matched runs or threads in a queue for human review, for example all traces with negative feedback. Adding to a dataset collects examples, and webhooks post to an external endpoint.

questions.title: Which metric types can LangSmith alerts be configured on?
questions.explanation: Alerts support Run Count, Cost, Errors, Feedback Score and Latency. Hardware metrics such as GPU utilization are not alert metrics.

questions.title: A webhook alert's request body template contains the placeholder {alert_rule_name}, and the receiving service does not parse the JSON. What is delivered?

options.text: LangSmith replaces the placeholder with the alert rule name
The placeholder is sent verbatim, while the alert fields are merged into the JSON as top-level keys
The webhook is rejected by LangSmith as invalid
The alert fields are dropped when a template is present

questions.explanation: LangSmith does not perform template substitution on the body; auto-populated fields such as alert_rule_name and project_name are added as top-level keys. A placeholder only resolves if the receiver itself extracts fields from the JSON.

questions.title: The model price table has input at $2 per 1M tokens, cache_read input at $1 per 1M tokens and output at $3 per 1M tokens. What total cost does LangSmith compute for this usage_metadata?
questions.explanation: Cost is computed from the most specific token type: 5 cache_read tokens at $1/1M plus the remaining 15 input tokens at $2/1M gives $3.5e-5, and 10 output tokens at $3/1M gives $3e-5, totaling $6.5e-5. Pricing all input at the default rate would wrongly give $7.0e-5.

questions.title: Which metadata key lets LangSmith match a custom model's token counts to a price in the model pricing table?
questions.explanation: The match pattern in the pricing table is applied to ls_model_name (and the provider to ls_provider) in the run metadata. Token counts and a price entry are also required to compute cost.

questions.title: Which custom dashboard metric lets you define a numerator and a denominator, each with its own filter, for example to chart an error rate?
questions.explanation: Ratio combines two metrics, each with its own filter, which suits error rate or LLM run share. Count only totals runs matching one filter.

questions.title: You want dashboard charts for both traces and LLM calls grouped by the same metadata key. What do the docs recommend?

options.text: Attach the metadata only to the root run; it propagates to children
Attach the metadata only to the LLM runs; it propagates to the root
Attach the metadata to both the trace (root run) and the specific LLM runs
Use a tag instead, because tags propagate to all runs

questions.explanation: Metadata and tags are not propagated between parent and child runs, so each run level that you want to group by needs the metadata attached.
